{{Quote|We were so focused on perfecting the advanced sensor analysis of the XPLR-R, that we simply ignored our needs in corporate defense.|Former VSIS president [[Rina Fio]] after the takeover|<ref name="Sensor Technology Dispute Settled in Takeover" />}}
The '''XPLR-R''' was a prototype [[Explorer droid/Legends|hyperspace-route-mapping and habitation-location unit]] developed by [[Viper Sensor Intelligence Systems]]. During the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]], rival [[Arakyd Industries/Legends|Arakyd Industries]] asserted that the XPLR-R borrowed heavily from the proprietary designs of their [[Probe droid/Legends|probe droid]] line. As a result, Arakyd demanded aggressive remuneration and technology rights of the younger firm and the two companies entered an 18-[[Standard month/Legends|month]]-long dispute. However, VSIS was so focused on perfecting the XPLR-R's advanced sensor analysis that it ignored its needs in corporate defense.<ref name="Sensor Technology Dispute Settled in Takeover" />

Shortly before the outbreak of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] in the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]],<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|I|4|AAD-4}}</ref> the dispute over the XPLR-R was resolved when Arakyd absorbed its smaller competitor in an armed takeover<ref name="TNEGTD">''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref> of [[Viper Tower]] and kept VSIS in operation as a research-and-development division.<ref name="Sensor Technology Dispute Settled in Takeover" /> In possession of proprietary Viper technology, Arakyd released the [[Viper probe droid/Legends|Viper probe droid]], the company's biggest success to date.<ref name="TNEGTD" />

==Behind the scenes==
The XPLR-R was originally created for ''[[HoloNet News Vol. 531 50]]'', a [[HoloNet News (original website)|HoloNet News]] article written by [[Pablo Hidalgo]] and [[Paul Ens]] with illustrations by [[Joe Corroney]] and released on [[April 4]], [[2002]].<ref name="Sensor Technology Dispute Settled in Takeover" />
